summary: The Files tab starts at "This computer /": Home under it, open and selected at start; Drives (S4, udisks2) right under Home, near the top, each drive and its mounted volume as a folder; the other folders of / collapsed; /proc, /sys, /dev and /run shown as "· system" rows and never read (no listing, no id, never on the board); dot-names hidden with a "Show hidden" switch in the tab's header; Graphite's workspace shown where it lives in Home with Graphite's mark; the Desk drawer stays as L1 built it (the Files drawer gave way to the computer). Folders are read lazily, one level when opened (at most 400 rows). L1's ids extend to any path lazily (objects.get {path: "/…" or "~/…"} makes the id of that one file when it is focused, opened or linked); the board focuses a file anywhere (FILE/FOLDER tile, its place in words, possible links). Kas's reach (workbench/home_reach.py, enforced in the Kernel's path): reads anywhere the account can read (system folders never); her changes (K1 steps, K2 file tools, her hand's cards in Talk, K6 Apply) only inside Home or the workspace's Files, under grants as before, never outside: "outside your home: never" at every place of the dial; a K3 grant's folder may be any folder in Home ("~/Rail notes"), never outside it, never all of Home, never Graphite's own records or program; the owner's own press follows the system's permissions anywhere.

decisions: Drives is a row under "This computer /", right after Home, not a separate top-level row: with / listed under This computer a top-level Drives row ended up 30 rows down; under Home it stays near the top. Drives is open at start.

At start the tree lands on Home (open, selected, scrolled to the top) and the board keeps its own start: L1's first sync (via "start") no longer reveals the board's focus in the tree. Once the owner chooses anything, tree and board share the selection as before.

A path argument named from / or ~ is that path on the computer; a path with no leading / or ~ is inside Files as before (files_service.resolve). An absolute path inside Files is the Files path it is (its rules apply).

Areas (home_reach.area): files (the workspace's Files, its own rules, Slate as before), own (the workspace's records folder outside Files and Graphite's program: never hers as files, even under a grant), home, system (/proc /sys /dev /run; /run/media is treated as a drive place, not a system folder), outside.

Her work is: a grant permit in force (K1 step, K2 tool use), her hand's card in Talk (shell2.run_staged now runs inside home_reach.hers(): a card she does by the dial needs a grant in force for Home outside Files; one you Approve reaches its own targets in Home; outside Home never), or a principal without approve. Anything else is your own press: outside Home it follows the system's permissions (Graphite asks for nothing more).

The "outside your home: never" check runs before any grant or press is asked for: grants.check_step raises it (the step is blocked with exactly those words), grants.authorise blocks the runner's next step with it (no one-press grant offered), tools_registry._pre_files and check_tool say it, files_service.may_change enforces it at dispatch, sandbox.apply refuses it.
Versions of a Home file are kept in Files/.versions/~home/<path in Home> (~root/ outside Home), so Undo/revert work as for Files.
Find and smart folders stay inside Files (FILES_FIND_IN_FILES): a search from / would scan the disk.

Objects outside Files are kept in L1's store under their whole resolved path; a reading of Files never marks them missing; renames outside Files are found by inode at the next objects.get (no watcher outside Files). L1's full reading of Files itself is unchanged.
depths._place (L4, used by A1) keeps refusing an id outside Files (REVISIONS_OUTSIDE), so revisions and A1 sessions stay Files-only as their slices built them.
A folder on the board is a FOLDER tile (board_model.file_object), Files folders included; a file outside Files says where it is in words (in ~/Rail notes).
No Kernel operation, schema or scope changed: tools/record_registry.py --check on the copy reported no differences, so docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json was not regenerated.
findings_for_the_coordinator: Patch applies cleanly (git apply --check) to the base bed61f2 and to current main claude/epic-galileo-c7k11y (workbench/ and tests_integrated/).

A1 (app_files, merged on main after my base) and K9: any file change of hers they make should run inside home_reach.hers(op, args, pressed=...) or check home_reach.her_change(kernel, path) first; A1's open path stays Files-only through depths._place.
Search's CABINET section no longer lists every file of Files by name (the Files drawer is gone; computer rows exist only for opened folders). Search's Files part still finds them.
The centre is empty at start in these frames (no board until something is focused): D1's empty state ("the board shows Home with one line") would fit well with the tree landing on Home.

The tree reads each opened folder again on the cabinet's 2.5 s refresh (one level, at most 400 rows); the drives are read at most every 10 s through machine_room_qt.reading (S4's shared cache), on the window's thread.
Right-click on a computer row gets the cabinet tree's generic entries (and Open with for a file); rename/move/trash of Home files from the tree is not offered yet.
K2's tool words still say "in Files"; she can name ~/… paths in their arguments.
not_done: Nothing tested in the owner's sense; nothing ran on the ThinkPad. Existing tests and window checks not run (the owner's rule).
No watcher outside Files: a rename in Home by another program updates the tree on its next reading and the id on the next objects.get, not the open breadcrumb at once.
Owner actions on Home files from the tree (rename, move, DELETE) are not added; the Kernel ops accept ~/ paths for the owner already.
K6 sandbox inputs stay inside Files; A1 sessions stay inside Files.
release_note: The Files tab starts at "This computer /": Home is open and chosen at start, Drives stands right under it, and every other folder your account can read is one click away (system folders like /proc are shown but never read; names that start with a dot appear with Show hidden). Graphite's own workspace sits in Home like any folder, marked with Graphite's sign, and its records stay in the Desk drawer. Any file can be put on the board. Kasandra may read wherever you can; what she changes stays inside your home, under your grants, and a step aimed outside it stops with "outside your home: never", whatever the dial says.
